answer.rationale: Finance mandates 18% unit-cost reduction, the low-cost vendor's quoted price meets the mandate on its own, and the contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew — so the decision must be made now, and going with the incumbent cannot satisfy the mandate without trade-offs elsewhere. Memory_c2 documents that this same vendor was previously used as primary with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing, which lowers the execution risk of a switch. Memory_c6 confirms that once we're committed to a primary supplier, longer terms unlock further volume pricing — so I would negotiate a multi-year commitment with the low-cost vendor to push unit cost below the mandate, not just meet it. Rather than a full cutover of all volume on day 71, I would run a small guarded pilot for the first cycle (e.g., a single line or limited lot) to confirm the low-cost vendor can sustain delivery before scaling, since memory_c2 is point-in-time evidence, not a guarantee. This preserves cost improvement, protects delivery risk on the line running at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, and keeps negotiating leverage with the incumbent as a fallback. Note: I am downgrading confidence below my prior — a full immediate switch on a single decision carries tail risk I cannot fully verify within this cycle, so I recommend the guarded variant rather than committing the entire primary spend.
